result.summary: This PR replaces memcpy with std::copy in CHMAC_SHA256 and CHMAC_SHA512 so that empty HMAC keys no longer trigger a UBSan null-pointer warning, since std::copy has defined semantics for empty ranges while memcpy does not. It adds empty-key HMAC test vectors, lets the crypto fuzz target pass empty byte vectors directly instead of resizing them away, and removes a now-stale empty-input guard in the eval_script fuzz target since ConsumeRemainingBytes() already handles the empty case safely.
result.problem: UBSan flags memcpy(dst, nullptr, 0) as passing a null pointer even though the copy length is zero, which previously forced the crypto and eval_script fuzz harnesses to avoid or special-case empty inputs, reducing fuzz coverage of the empty-key/empty-input path.

The fix is correct and confirmed to produce identical assembly via godbolt, but the underlying issue was a sanitizer nuisance rather than a functional or security bug, keeping it in the worthwhile-but-deferrable band.

result.card: This PR replaces memcpy with std::copy in CHMAC_SHA256 and CHMAC_SHA512 to fix a UBSan null-pointer warning triggered by empty HMAC keys, since memcpy(dst, nullptr, 0) is technically undefined while std::copy handles empty ranges cleanly. It also removes now-unnecessary empty-input workarounds in the crypto and eval_script fuzz targets, improving their coverage of empty inputs. Reviewer maflcko suggested the std::copy approach and pushed for a cleaner commit message, both of which the author (also a project member) implemented, and reviewer sedited gave a plain ACK. The PR is small, ready for merge, has no open objections, and carries no dependencies on other PRs. Its impact is a minor correctness and test-hygiene fix in shared crypto utility code rather than a user-facing or security-critical change.
